resources.string: Device-level debugging for developers. Takes effect immediately once enabled; no per-call confirmation.
Full ADB client inside the sandbox (shell privileges, can drive external devices)
USB debugging is off. Open Settings → Developer options and enable it, then turn this channel on.

The first connection must be confirmed on the phone ("Allow debugging"). That grant is stored by the phone OS (Developer options → Revoke USB debugging authorizations clears it); turning this switch off only disconnects DSHBox and does not delete the grant.
The access code is locked after too many failed attempts. Regenerate it below to allow connections again.
This device is not rooted; this channel is unavailable.

No executable su found on this device. The root channel needs a rooted device (Magisk / KernelSU / APatch and similar) whose root manager does not hide su from this app (for example Magisk’s DenyList or Hide app). Without root or authorization the switch stays disabled and the executor never starts; the settings below can still be viewed and pre-set.
Unix socket (this app and the sandbox only)

Once enabled, any device on the same network can connect to this phone\'s ADB service and obtain the device shell (uid 2000) — installing apps, reading files, running commands. Use only on a trusted network.
Once enabled, any app on this device that obtains the access code can run commands as root on this device. Enable only when an external tool needs to connect.

Once enabled, any device on the same network that obtains the access code can run commands as root on this device. Traffic is unencrypted, so others on the network may see command content and output. Use only on a fully trusted network and make sure the access code has not leaked.
This port is already in use, possibly by an adb you installed yourself or another program. Choose a custom port or stop that program (this app never terminates other processes).
Unapplied changes; the running configuration is still %1$s
This feature requires the sandbox to be running
Pairing needs the ADB channel: turn on ADB access above first (that switch creates the key and the adb entry point).
The Wireless debugging screen shows IP address and port; copy it here (e.g. 192.168.1.5:37123).
① Open Settings → Developer options → Wireless debugging on the phone and stay on that page (leaving it refreshes the pairing code).
Next step shows the 6-digit code field; if auto-discovery fails you can type the pairing address yourself.
② In Wireless debugging, tap "Pair device with pairing code"; a 6-digit code appears.
Use split screen (phone settings on one side, stay on that page; DSHBox on the other) or put DSHBox in a floating window. Leaving the Wireless debugging page refreshes the code.
③ Enter the 6-digit code below (pairing starts as soon as it is complete):
This device is now in "Paired devices". Future connections will not ask for authorization again.
The pairing code only exists in the phone settings; the connection address above is what can be copied here.
Shown in the "Pair device with pairing code" dialog
Runs adb connect; on first connection the device shows the standard \"Allow debugging\" dialog. No pairing code needed — use it for devices already authorized, or with a fixed tcpip port.
Enter the IP address and port shown in Wireless debugging
The device has not authorized this computer yet. Allow the debugging prompt on the device, then tap Connect again.
Cannot reach that address: check the IP/port and that TCP debugging is enabled on the device.
Scan the QR code with the external tool, or copy the code
Regenerating invalidates the previous access code immediately; external tools already configured must be updated.
Local identity and paired devices; the key is what DSH and external tools use to reach devices.
No keys yet. One is generated automatically on the first device connection.
No paired devices yet. They appear here after you pair one.
Pairing records exist but contain no readable device identifier.
Pairing records contain device identifiers only; the adb file provides no pairing time or method.
Read from the sandbox with adb devices — the same server DSH uses.
⚠ Deleting the local key makes every device need re-pairing; the phone\'s "authorized computers" records remain.
Could not enable ADB: runtime assets are missing or extraction failed.
ADB is installed, but USB debugging is off on the phone. Open Settings → Developer options and enable USB debugging; otherwise no device can be connected.
ADB is installed. The server starts with the sandbox; once it runs you can use adb directly in the terminal.
Disconnected. The phone still keeps the "Allow debugging" grant; to clear it, open Settings → Developer options → Revoke USB debugging authorizations.
Applied: %1$s (stopped %2$d old server(s); the next call rebuilds it)
Applied and restarted the root executor
Applied (root channel is off, nothing to restart)
Configuration applied, but the executor could not start on the new setting: socket or port in use.
Root executor started, but android-root could not be installed (the CLI directory is read-only). Turn the switch off and on again.
Delete failed: the file may be in use.
Local key deleted. Every device must be paired again; the phone\'s "authorized computers" records remain — open Settings → Developer options → Revoke USB debugging authorizations to clear them.
Key deleted; the matching device must be paired again.
Generation failed: the ADB channel must be on and the sandbox running.
Pairing records cleared. The local identity is kept, so reconnecting will not ask for authorization.
su exists but authorization was not granted (or the prompt timed out). Allow DSHBox in your root manager and try again.
No wireless-debugging pairing service found. Make sure Wireless debugging is on and stay on that page, then retry.
Paired, but the automatic connection failed. Read the IP and port on the phone Wireless debugging screen and enter them below.
The connection address must look like ip:port.
Wrong or expired pairing code. Please get a new one.
Cannot reach that address: check that both devices are on the same network and Wireless debugging is on.
Enter the pairing address and port first.
This device is not rooted; the root channel cannot be enabled.
Root executor failed to start: socket or port in use.
Access code updated; external tools already configured must be updated.
The phone keeps the "Allow debugging" grant. Turning this switch off only disconnects DSHBox; to clear the grant, open Settings → Developer options → Revoke USB debugging authorizations.

ADB and Root here are full-capability channels: turning a switch on is the authorization. They do not go through the assistant channel’s safety gate (per-call approval, capability table, quotas, audit). The two channels are independent and keep working even when the assistant channel is fully off.
When enabled, a complete adb is installed inside the sandbox (/opt/elevation/bin/adb); when disabled it is removed, and both the command and its connections stop working.
The panel and DSH use the same file (/opt/elevation/server.conf): a change on either side applies to both, and Apply stops the old server and restarts it with the new settings.

Pairing code: in Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code, read the IP:port and the 6-digit code. That screen expires once you leave it, so keep it visible in split screen or a floating window.
Direct connect: for a device already paired or authorized, just enter IP:port. The first connection may still need "Allow debugging" on that device.

This is a complete adb client inside the sandbox, not a restricted proxy: it can debug this phone (wireless debugging must be on) and other devices on your LAN; other apps or tools on this phone can also gain ADB access through this server.

Cautions: LAN mode is plaintext, so content is visible on the same network; keys and authorizations live in the app’s private storage, so uninstalling or clearing data loses them and you must pair again.
When enabled, android-root <command> runs as Android root inside the sandbox (the device must be rooted and must grant access). When disabled the executor stops and the command disappears.

Root settings live only in the app’s private storage: the sandbox and DSH cannot read or change them. DSH can only run commands (through root.sock); transport, port and access code are yours to view and change here.

Cautions: the access code is root access itself - leaking it hands over the device, never share it, and regenerate it immediately if you suspect a leak. Repeated failures lock the channel; regenerating the code unlocks it. LAN mode is plaintext as well.
A device without root cannot enable this channel: the switch stays disabled, but the settings below can still be viewed and pre-set.
The saved port (%1$s) was invalid and has been reset to the default 5037.
